culture: The Jardín is the central town square, where people gather, especially in the evening
Taxi stands are often located by the main square (Jardín)
The streets of the Centro are cobblestone, so taxis go slowly uphill
The Parroquia is a famous pink church with tall towers, two blocks from the Jardín
The Parroquia has colorful stained glass windows inside
The Parroquia's towers are lit with golden lights at night
In the evening the Jardín fills with families and mariachis
Cobblestone streets date from the colonial era, giving the Centro an old, beautiful look
Common polite phrases: "suba con confianza" (get in, don't hesitate), "Me dio gusto" (it was a pleasure), "Que le vaya muy bien" (take care)
"ahorita" means right now / in a little while
"cuadras" are city blocks, used for giving distances
"vámonos" means let's go
"despacito" means nice and slowly
"pueblo" refers to a town, and locals take pride in its most famous landmark
